key_insight: Turbulent coherent structures are framed as universal thermodynamic responses to energy-throughput imbalance, with a computable order parameter (Π) distinguishing near-equilibrium fluctuations from far-from-equilibrium dissipative structures.
engineering_relevance: This could provide a physics-based criterion for when CFD must resolve coherent flow structures, improving model fidelity and reducing ambiguous mesh or closure choices in driven dissipative flows.
method: Recasts turbulence through renormalized Navier-Stokes equations and non-equilibrium statistical physics.
Introduces an effective thermodynamic order parameter (Π) to identify coherent structures.
Classifies coherence by access to bifurcations: transient adjustment vs autonomous dissipative state.
evidence_signal: The abstract claims a foundational theoretical framework and a computable order parameter, but it does not report numerical experiments, datasets, or benchmark validation results.
watch_item: The framework appears highly conceptual in the abstract, so practical adoption will depend on how Π is computed robustly and validated across real turbulent flows.
paper_title: Coherence as Thermodynamic Organization: Toward a Non-Equilibrium Turbulence Theory
